sources.inspection: Transcription note, title/preface and eleven bounded passages read in full: Grand Gulf and the Haines' Bluff feint (OCR pp.122–127), Port Gibson (127–132), Raymond (142–143), Jackson (146–148), Big Black (161–164), the siege works and garrison (174–177), the May 22 assault result (184–185), Union reinforcement (188), the garrison before surrender (200–201), surrender terms and paroles (204–207) and Helena (234–236). Several running heads are misprinted in OCR (128 as '123', 148 as '118', 164 as '161'); locators use an explicit marker map.

sources.author: Andrew A. Humphreys
sources.edition: New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, 1883, per catalog and OCR title; not checked against print.
sources.archival_identifier: Internet Archive cu31924030917177; Cornell University Library; digitized 2006 with Microsoft funding
sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface is signed June 1883 in OCR; that date is not assigned to narrative passages.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Andrew A. Humphreys, styled on the title page 'CHIEF OF STAFF ARMY OF THE POTOMAC' and in the publisher's list in the same OCR 'Chief of Staff, Army of the Potomac, 1863-64'; the start date of that role is not established in the inspected pages. An interested participant account. By his preface the Secretary of War made the Department's papers accessible to him, and he thanks Col. Scott, then preparing the Official Records for publication; Volume XXVII was printed in 1889, after this book, so any dependence is on shared underlying papers, not the printed compilation. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished.

sources.author: Andrew A. Humphreys
sources.edition: New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, 1883 (Campaigns of the Civil War, XII), per catalog and OCR title; not checked against print.
sources.archival_identifier: Internet Archive virginiacampaign00hump_0; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; scanned 2018
sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface in OCR is signed but undated; the 1883 imprint is not assigned to narrative passages as a composition date.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Andrew A. Humphreys, styled on the OCR title page 'CHIEF OF STAFF, ARMY OF THE POTOMAC' and 'COMMANDING SECOND CORPS'. Same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan (Cornell scan cu31924030917177): this book is placed in that author's existing independence group, humphreys-gettysburg-rapidan-1883, whose name reflects the earlier volume; the two books are not independent of each other. An interested participant account. By his preface the War Department's reports, returns, orders and despatches were placed at his disposal, and he used the retained copies of Meade's despatches and his own papers; Sheridan's dispatches printed in Official Records XXXVI Part 1 are addressed to him as chief of staff. It therefore shares headquarters papers with the Meade and Sheridan families and is not independent of them. Confederate reports, diaries and memoirs he quotes are not separately inspected. Volume XXXVI was printed in 1891, after this book. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished.

sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface is dated New York, January, 1883; that date is not assigned to narrative passages as a composition date.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by George E. Pond, styled on the OCR title page 'ASSOCIATE EDITOR OF THE ARMY AND NAVY JOURNAL'; not shown as a participant in the inspected passages. By his preface he studied the official documents at the War Records Office and made free use of field despatches, many then unpublished. He quotes Wallace's, Crook's, Wright's, Sheridan's, Torbert's and Early's reports and despatches, so this history is not independent of the Official Records families selected in this pass. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished. No earlier registry group for this author.

sources.author: Jacob D. Cox

sources.archival_identifier: Internet Archive atlantabyjacobcox09jcoxrich; University of California Libraries (call number ucb:GLAD-134274165); scanned 2006 with MSN sponsorship
sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative published 1882; no preface or signed date in the OCR. The publication year is not assigned to narrative passages as a document or event date.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Jacob D. Cox, styled on the title page 'LATE MAJOR-GENERAL COMMANDING TWENTY THIRD ARMY CORPS'. In the selected narrative his own command appears in the third person as Cox's division of the Twenty-third Corps, and he temporarily commanded that corps after Schofield's injury on May 25-26. An interested participant account written from the Union side. The text cites official reports (for example Thomas's, Geary's, Howard's and Logan's), Sherman's despatches and Memoirs, Johnston's Narrative, Hood's Advance and Retreat and the Southern Historical Society Papers, and Appendix A rests on Major E. C. Dawes's research in the Confederate returns; it is therefore not independent of those papers or memoirs. Official Records Volume XXXVIII was printed in 1891, after this book, so any dependence is on shared underlying papers, not the printed compilation. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished.

sources.author: Jacob D. Cox
sources.edition: New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, 1882 (Campaigns of the Civil War, X), per OCR title page ('CAMPAIGNS OF THE CIVIL IVAK.—X', 'CHARLES SCRIBNER'S SONS 1882') and catalog; preface signed 'CINCINNATI, September, 1882'. Not checked against print.
sources.archival_identifier: Internet Archive marchtoseafrankl00coxjuoft; Robarts Library, University of Toronto; scanned 2007
sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface is dated September 1882; that date and the 1882 imprint are not assigned to narrative passages as composition dates or as contemporary knowledge.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Jacob D. Cox, styled on the OCR title page 'LATE MAJOK-GENERAL COMMANDING TWENTY-THIRD ARMY CORPS'. He commanded a division and, at Franklin, both divisions of the Twenty-third Corps under Schofield, so for Columbia, Spring Hill, Franklin and Nashville it is an interested participant account. By his preface he had access to unpublished War Records Office archives and official information, and he cites Hood's, Bate's, Walthall's, Beauregard's and Schofield's reports and statements, Jordan and Pryor's Campaigns of Forrest (registered as jordan-pryor-forrest-1868) and C. C. Jones's Siege of Savannah; it therefore shares official papers with the Official Records families and is not independent of them. His own report and journal printed in Official Records XLV part 1 (Nos. 97 and 98) were not inspected; any later use of them belongs to this author family. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished. Cox's earlier volume Atlanta is not registered in this pass.
sources.rights: Underlying 1882 book is public domain in the United States. Public catalog metadata and full OCR retained; no print scans or maps downloaded.

sources.archival_identifier: Internet Archive marchtoseafrankl00coxjuoft; Robarts Library, University of Toronto; scanned 2007
sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface is dated September 1882; that date and the 1882 imprint are not assigned to narrative passages as composition dates or as contemporary knowledge.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Jacob D. Cox, styled on the OCR title page 'LATE MAJOK-GENERAL COMMANDING TWENTY-THIRD ARMY CORPS'. He commanded a division and, at Franklin, both divisions of the Twenty-third Corps under Schofield, so for Columbia, Spring Hill, Franklin and Nashville it is an interested participant account. By his preface he had access to unpublished War Records Office archives and official information, and he cites Hood's, Bate's, Walthall's, Beauregard's and Schofield's reports and statements, Jordan and Pryor's Campaigns of Forrest (registered as jordan-pryor-forrest-1868) and C. C. Jones's Siege of Savannah; it therefore shares official papers with the Official Records families and is not independent of them. His own report and journal printed in Official Records XLV part 1 (Nos. 97 and 98) were not inspected; any later use of them belongs to this author family. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished. Cox's earlier volume Atlanta is not registered in this pass.
sources.rights: Underlying 1882 book is public domain in the United States. Public catalog metadata and full OCR retained; no print scans or maps downloaded.

Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished. No earlier registry group for this author.

sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Jacob D. Cox, styled on the title page 'LATE MAJOR-GENERAL COMMANDING TWENTY THIRD ARMY CORPS'. In the selected narrative his own command appears in the third person as Cox's division of the Twenty-third Corps, and he temporarily commanded that corps after Schofield's injury on May 25-26. An interested participant account written from the Union side. The text cites official reports (for example Thomas's, Geary's, Howard's and Logan's), Sherman's despatches and Memoirs, Johnston's Narrative, Hood's Advance and Retreat and the Southern Historical Society Papers, and Appendix A rests on Major E. C. Dawes's research in the Confederate returns; it is therefore not independent of those papers or memoirs. Official Records Volume XXXVIII was printed in 1891, after this book, so any dependence is on shared underlying papers, not the printed compilation. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished.

sources.author: Andrew A. Humphreys
sources.edition: New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, 1883 (Campaigns of the Civil War, XII), per catalog and OCR title; not checked against print.
sources.archival_identifier: Internet Archive virginiacampaign00hump_0; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; scanned 2018
sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface in OCR is signed but undated; the 1883 imprint is not assigned to narrative passages as a composition date.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Andrew A. Humphreys, styled on the OCR title page 'CHIEF OF STAFF, ARMY OF THE POTOMAC' and 'COMMANDING SECOND CORPS'. Same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan (Cornell scan cu31924030917177): this book is placed in that author's existing independence group, humphreys-gettysburg-rapidan-1883, whose name reflects the earlier volume; the two books are not independent of each other. An interested participant account. By his preface the War Department's reports, returns, orders and despatches were placed at his disposal, and he used the retained copies of Meade's despatches and his own papers; Sheridan's dispatches printed in Official Records XXXVI Part 1 are addressed to him as chief of staff. It therefore shares headquarters papers with the Meade and Sheridan families and is not independent of them. Confederate reports, diaries and memoirs he quotes are not separately inspected. Volume XXXVI was printed in 1891, after this book. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished.
sources.rights: Underlying 1883 book is public domain in the United States. Public catalog metadata and full OCR retained, including library notices; no print scans or maps downloaded.

sources.inspection: Transcription note and seventeen passages read in full: the June 9 attempt on Petersburg (OCR pp.196–198); the June 15–18 assaults (pp.204–225); the June 21–23 Weldon Railroad movement (pp.226–229); the July 27–29 Deep Bottom movement (pp.247–250); the Petersburg mine and the July returns (pp.250–265); the August Deep Bottom movement (pp.268–272); Globe Tavern (pp.272–278); Reams's Station, August 25 (pp.278–283); Fort Harrison (pp.284–289); Peebles's Farm (pp.289–293); the October 7 and 13 actions (pp.293–294); the Boydton plank-road movement with Lee's despatches in footnote (pp.294–304); the Fair Oaks demonstration (pp.304–306); the winter returns (pp.308–309); Hatcher's Run (pp.311–315); Fort Stedman (pp.316–321); and the spring 1865 strengths (p.323). Chapter openings (pp.226, 284, 308) have no running head in OCR, and the p.268 head reads '2G8'; those locators are inferred. Also read but not selected: Chapter VII's opening (pp.194–204), Chapter VIII's Trevilian, Saint Mary's Church and Wilson-Kautz raid passages (pp.230–242) and Chapter XIII's opening (p.322).

sources.author: Wiley Britton

sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface is undated in OCR; the 1899 imprint is not assigned to narrative passages as a composition date.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Wiley Britton, styled on the OCR title page 'LATE OF THE WAR DEPARTMENT' and described as 'BASED UPON OFFICIAL REPORTS AND OBSERVATIONS OF THE AUTHOR'. By his preface the descriptions of the larger operations are mainly based on the published official reports, supplemented by his wartime diaries, depositions taken in later claims work, statements of participants and George S. Grover's manuscript notes on the Price Raid; he says he participated in the operations described. It is therefore not independent of the Official Records reports, including Price's, and it quotes Ewing's and Harding's reports and an 1896 article by T. J. Mackey. No earlier registry group for this author. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished.

sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Wiley Britton, styled on the OCR title page 'LATE OF THE WAR DEPARTMENT' and described as 'BASED UPON OFFICIAL REPORTS AND OBSERVATIONS OF THE AUTHOR'. By his preface the descriptions of the larger operations are mainly based on the published official reports, supplemented by his wartime diaries, depositions taken in later claims work, statements of participants and George S. Grover's manuscript notes on the Price Raid; he says he participated in the operations described. It is therefore not independent of the Official Records reports, including Price's, and it quotes Ewing's and Harding's reports and an 1896 article by T. J. Mackey. Same book, parent and group (`britton-civil-war-border-1899`) as the Camden selection; one witness family across both campaigns. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished.

sources.title: Andrew A. Humphreys, The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65: The Army of the Potomac and the Army of the James
sources.author: Andrew A. Humphreys
sources.edition: New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, 1883 (Campaigns of the Civil War, XII), per catalog and OCR title; not checked against print.
sources.archival_identifier: Internet Archive virginiacampaign00hump_0; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; scanned 2018
sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface in OCR is signed but undated; the 1883 imprint is not assigned to narrative passages as a composition date.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Andrew A. Humphreys, styled on the OCR title page 'CHIEF OF STAFF, ARMY OF THE POTOMAC' and 'COMMANDING SECOND CORPS'. Same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan (Cornell scan cu31924030917177): this book is placed in that author's existing independence group, humphreys-gettysburg-rapidan-1883, whose name reflects the earlier volume; the two books are not independent of each other. An interested participant account. By his preface the War Department's reports, returns, orders and despatches were placed at his disposal, and he used the retained copies of Meade's despatches and his own papers; Sheridan's dispatches printed in Official Records XXXVI Part 1 are addressed to him as chief of staff. It therefore shares headquarters papers with the Meade and Sheridan families and is not independent of them. Confederate reports, diaries and memoirs he quotes are not separately inspected. Volume XXXVI was printed in 1891, after this book. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished.
sources.rights: Underlying 1883 book is public domain in the United States. Public catalog metadata and full OCR retained, including library notices; no print scans or maps downloaded.
sources.snapshot_transform: Decode UTF-8 parent; select recorded half-open Unicode character ranges, collapse whitespace with split/join, preserve all other characters; add local headings and transcription note.
sources.inspection: Transcription note and thirteen passages read in full, covering Chapter XIII from its opening (OCR pp.322–323, up to the spring 1865 strengths already selected as humphreys-petersburg-selections-v1 section spring-1865-strengths, which is not repeated) to its end (pp.323–372), all of Chapter XIV (pp.373–400) and Appendix L on the March 31 and February 20, 1865 returns (pp.432–434). The chapter openings on pp.322 and 373 and the opening of Appendix L on p.432 have no running head in OCR, and the p.354 head reads '854'; those locators are inferred. Humphreys commanded the Second Corps throughout these passages. Also read but not selected: the list of commanders on March 31, 1865 that follows in Appendix L (pp.435–438). Appendix M (the Grant-Lee correspondence) was not inspected.

sources.document_date_note: Retrospective narrative. The preface is dated New York, January, 1883; that date is not assigned to narrative passages as a composition date.
sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by George E. Pond, styled on the OCR title page 'ASSOCIATE EDITOR OF THE ARMY AND NAVY JOURNAL'; not shown as a participant in the inspected passages. By his preface he studied the official documents at the War Records Office and made free use of field despatches, many then unpublished. He quotes Wallace's, Crook's, Wright's, Sheridan's, Torbert's and Early's reports and despatches, so this history is not independent of the Official Records families selected in this pass. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished. No earlier registry group for this author. For the Waynesboro passage Pond quotes and closely follows Sheridan's July 16, 1865 report (or46-1-sheridan-waynesborough-selections-v1), so the two are not independent.

sources.dependency_note: One retrospective history by Jacob D. Cox, styled on the OCR title page 'LATE MAJOK-GENERAL COMMANDING TWENTY-THIRD ARMY CORPS'. He commanded a division and, at Franklin, both divisions of the Twenty-third Corps under Schofield, so for Columbia, Spring Hill, Franklin and Nashville it is an interested participant account. By his preface he had access to unpublished War Records Office archives and official information, and he cites Hood's, Bate's, Walthall's, Beauregard's and Schofield's reports and statements, Jordan and Pryor's Campaigns of Forrest (registered as jordan-pryor-forrest-1868) and C. C. Jones's Siege of Savannah; it therefore shares official papers with the Official Records families and is not independent of them. His own report and journal printed in Official Records XLV part 1 (Nos. 97 and 98) were not inspected; any later use of them belongs to this author family. Relationship to later NPS summaries is unestablished. Cox's earlier volume Atlanta (Campaigns of the Civil War IX, 1882) is registered as ia-cox-atlanta-metadata-v1, cox-atlanta-ocr-v1 and cox-atlanta-selections-v1 (superseded by the metadata-only cox-atlanta-selections-v2); following the Humphreys precedent, this book is placed in that author's existing group, cox-atlanta-1882, whose name reflects the earlier volume. The two books are one author family, not independent witnesses.

sources.inspection: Transcription note and two passages read in full: title and preface (front matter), and the Kinston narrative in Chapter IX, from the choice of New Berne as a base through Cox's discussion of numbers and losses (OCR pp.154–162). Also read for this pass but not selected: the preceding Wilmington passage and the rest of Chapter IX to the Goldsboro junction (pp.154, 162–163), Chapter X from its opening through the Salkehatchie crossing and the march to the Saluda (pp.163–172; no Rivers' Bridge narrative; pp.172–177 not read), Chapter XI's Monroe's Cross Roads, Averasboro and Bentonville passages (pp.177–194), and Appendix E (strength in the Carolinas, pp.239–243; tables partly garbled in OCR). Cox directed the Union forces at Kinston, so this passage is an interested participant account; he cites Johnston's Narrative and Beauregard for Confederate numbers. His Official Records report on the same operations is registered as or47-1-cox-kinston-selections-v1 (superseded by the metadata-only or47-1-cox-kinston-selections-v2) in the same author family.

sources.dependency_note: Dispatch of June 27, reports of July 3 and July 14, an undated casualty statement for the June 28 assault, and the report of October 2, 1863 by the Confederate brigade commander; interested accounts. Irwin's history quotes and cites these reports, so it is not independent of this family. No earlier registry group for this author. Shared OR container with the other selections from the same volume; later NPS dependence is unestablished.
sources.snapshot_transform: Decode UTF-8 parent; select recorded half-open Unicode character ranges, collapse whitespace with split/join, preserve all other characters; add local headings and transcription note.
sources.inspection: Title and Green's No. 15 reports (pp.225-232) and No. 6 report (pp.329-332) read in full. Selected: the June 27 dispatch to Mouton (p.226); the July 3 report on Donaldsonville (pp.227-229); its casualty statement (p.230; section key names the assault date, and the statement's own date is not printed, so it is mapped null); the July 14 report on the action of July 13 (pp.230-232); and the October 2 report on Stirling's Plantation with its casualty inclosure (pp.329-332). The June 30 report on Brashear City and Taylor's indorsements of July 6 and August 9 were read but not selected; they are Taylor's, not Green's.
